AI Footprint Tracker's original code is licensed under the MIT License. Dependencies and data keep their own licences and notices. The tables below are generated from `THIRD-PARTY-INVENTORY.json`, which records the exact installed versions and declared licence expressions; `SBOM.cdx.json` lists the same components and data in CycloneDX format. Data whose licence could not be verified says so.

Tokenizer vocabulary assets are redistributed only with the notices in `packages/tokenizers/LICENSES/`. A tokenizer mapping is a reproducibility dependency, not evidence that a consumer website exposed complete usage.

Local file extraction uses Mozilla PDF.js, fflate, saxes and xmlchars, with core-js code bundled by PDF.js. Their notices, including the PDF.js notices for its bundled fonts, colour profiles and image decoders, are preserved in each browser package. These parsers run locally; their inclusion does not imply provider OCR, rendered document visibility or complete request usage coverage.

## Website

The website build lists the components it ships, with their full licence texts, on its open-source page. The build fails if it bundles a package that the list does not include.

- ADEME Base Empreinte electricity factors: Abiotic resource depletion and primary energy factors of electricity. Licence not recorded here; check the Base Empreinte terms of use.
- BoaviztAPI server impact data: Server embodied impacts and non-GPU server power, as values in the EcoLogits data. No BoaviztAPI software is included. Licence of the values not recorded here.
- Bricolage Grotesque font files: WOFF2 subsets bundled into the extension and the website. The OFL copyright notice and licence travel with them: in licenses/ of each browser package and in the website's open-source page.
- EcoLogits model, provider and electricity data: Converted from the pinned EcoLogits release (packages/ecologits-core/upstream/lock.json) and distributed under MPL-2.0 with the port. The server uses the same data through the EcoLogits Python package. The entries marked as part of this data name the sources EcoLogits credits.
- EcoLogits reference coefficients for the archived Original method: Coefficients and default settings copied from the pinned EcoLogits source for the archived Original method, which the product no longer offers. The data still ships in the estimator bundle.
- Instrument Sans font files: WOFF2 subsets bundled into the extension and the website. The OFL copyright notice and licence travel with them: in licenses/ of each browser package and in the website's open-source page.
- Jegham et al. video generation figures: Video generation durations and server power. Published figures cited by EcoLogits; licence not recorded here.
- Lees-Perasso et al. GPU life-cycle study: GPU embodied impacts. Published figures cited by EcoLogits; licence not recorded here.
- ML.ENERGY Leaderboard measurements behind the EcoLogits regressions: EcoLogits ships regression coefficients fitted to these measurements, not the measurements themselves. Licence not recorded here: the leaderboard repository (https://github.com/ml-energy/leaderboard) had no licence file when checked on 9 September 2026.
- OpenRouter model statistics: Time to first token and output speed in the EcoLogits model records. Licence not recorded here.
- Our World in Data electricity mix: Electricity-mix carbon intensity. Our World in Data states that data it republishes from third parties stays under the original authors' terms.
- Schneider et al. TPU embodied carbon figures: TPU embodied carbon. Published figures cited by EcoLogits; licence not recorded here.
- World Resources Institute electricity water data: Water consumed to generate electricity (off-site WUE). Licence not recorded here; check the WRI publication terms.
- cl100k_base BPE ranks: Vocabulary shipped inside the MIT-licensed gpt-tokenizer package. It reproduces the cl100k_base encoding that OpenAI publishes with tiktoken (MIT); that notice is kept in packages/tokenizers/LICENSES. No separate licence for the rank files themselves is recorded.
- o200k_base BPE ranks: Vocabulary shipped inside the MIT-licensed gpt-tokenizer package. It reproduces the o200k_base encoding that OpenAI publishes with tiktoken (MIT); that notice is kept in packages/tokenizers/LICENSES. No separate licence for the rank files themselves is recorded.

The headline footprint excludes embodied impacts, but the bundled EcoLogits data contains them.

## EcoLogits

The estimator includes an independent TypeScript port derived from EcoLogits source files. EcoLogits is developed by its contributors and is part of CodeCarbon (https://github.com/mlco2/ecologits). The derived files remain under MPL-2.0 and keep their `SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0` headers; files that adapt a specific EcoLogits module name it in a "Derived from EcoLogits" line. Project-authored wrappers do not relicense them. The corresponding source is `packages/ecologits-core` in the public repository and `source/ecologits-source.zip` in each browser package, which also carries the MPL-2.0 text, the notice and the citation file under `licenses/ecologits/`. The organization server uses the unmodified EcoLogits Python package, also under MPL-2.0.

The EcoLogits methodology documentation (https://ecologits.ai/latest/methodology/) is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The project's methodology page cites and links to it; it does not copy or relicense that documentation. EcoLogits asks users to cite this article: Rincé, S. and Banse, A. (2025). EcoLogits: Evaluating the Environmental Impacts of Generative AI. Journal of Open Source Software, 10(111), 7471. https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.07471

The data sources above follow the EcoLogits methodology (https://ecologits.ai/latest/methodology/llm_inference/ and https://ecologits.ai/latest/methodology/video_generation/). Parameter counts of closed models are EcoLogits' own estimates, not vendor figures.

## Provider names

Provider names identify compatibility targets. AI Footprint Tracker is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity, ML.ENERGY, EcoLogits or CodeCarbon.
